---- MODULE W4Od12m1p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, NULL, ADMIN

Cap == 3
MaxVer == 3

VARIABLES token, adminLock, stock, writer, ver
vars == <<token, adminLock, stock, writer, ver>>

\* A token circulates a ring of fridge terminals granting exclusive write
\* access to the shared blood stock; an admin can override the ring.
TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Nodes \cup {NULL}
    /\ adminLock \in BOOLEAN
    /\ stock \in 0..Cap
    /\ writer \in Nodes \cup {ADMIN, NULL}
    /\ ver \in 0..MaxVer

Init ==
    /\ token \in Nodes
    /\ adminLock = FALSE
    /\ stock = 0
    /\ writer = NULL
    /\ ver = 0

\* The token is passed on to another terminal on the ring.
PassToken(m) ==
    /\ adminLock = FALSE
    /\ token # NULL
    /\ m # token
    /\ token' = m
    /\ UNCHANGED <<adminLock, stock, writer, ver>>

\* The terminal holding the token writes the shared stock exclusively.
NodeWrite(n) ==
    /\ adminLock = FALSE
    /\ token = n
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ stock' = (stock + 1) % (Cap + 1)
    /\ writer' = n
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, adminLock>>

\* A privileged admin overrides the ring, revoking the token to seize
\* exclusive access.
AdminOverride ==
    /\ adminLock = FALSE
    /\ adminLock' = TRUE
    /\ token' = NULL
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, writer, ver>>

\* Under override the admin writes the shared stock exclusively.
AdminWrite ==
    /\ adminLock = TRUE
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ stock' = (stock + 1) % (Cap + 1)
    /\ writer' = ADMIN
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, adminLock>>

\* The admin releases the override and hands the token back to a terminal.
AdminRelease(n) ==
    /\ adminLock = TRUE
    /\ adminLock' = FALSE
    /\ token' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, writer, ver>>

\* The audit window rolls over so writes can resume.
Rollover ==
    /\ ver >= MaxVer
    /\ ver' = 0
    /\ stock' = 0
    /\ writer' = NULL
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, adminLock>>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Nodes : PassToken(m)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : NodeWrite(n)
    \/ AdminOverride
    \/ AdminWrite
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : AdminRelease(n)
    \/ Rollover

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost update via exclusive access: when the admin override is active the
\* ring token is always revoked, so a terminal and the admin can never both
\* hold write access at once and races that lose updates cannot occur.
ExclusiveAccess == adminLock => (token = NULL)
====

CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
    NULL = NULL
    ADMIN = ADMIN
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT ExclusiveAccess
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker lets a ring of fridge terminals update one shared
blood-stock record. A single token circulates the ring, and only the terminal
currently holding the token may write, giving exclusive access.

The token is passed from terminal to terminal around the ring (PassToken). The
terminal that holds the token writes the shared stock exclusively (NodeWrite). A
privileged supervisor can override the ring at any time: the override seizes
exclusive access and revokes the token from the ring (AdminOverride), after which
the admin writes the stock directly (AdminWrite). When finished, the admin
releases the override and hands the token back to a terminal (AdminRelease).
Once the audit window fills, it rolls over so writes can resume (Rollover).

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the admin override is active the ring token is revoked,
so a terminal and the admin can never both hold write access at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od1m2p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Flights, Slots, Parts, NULL

VARIABLES status, pend, yes, owner, active
vars == <<status, pend, yes, owner, active>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ status \in [Slots -> {"free", "proposed", "committed"}]
  /\ pend \in [Slots -> Flights \cup {NULL}]
  /\ yes \in [Slots -> SUBSET Parts]
  /\ owner \in [Slots -> Flights \cup {NULL}]
  /\ active \in SUBSET Slots

Init ==
  /\ status = [s \in Slots |-> "free"]
  /\ pend = [s \in Slots |-> NULL]
  /\ yes = [s \in Slots |-> {}]
  /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> NULL]
  /\ active = Slots

FlightBusy(f) ==
  \/ \E s \in Slots : owner[s] = f
  \/ \E s \in Slots : pend[s] = f

Propose(s, f) ==
  /\ s \in active
  /\ status[s] = "free"
  /\ ~FlightBusy(f)
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![s] = "proposed"]
  /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![s] = f]
  /\ yes' = [yes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, active>>

Vote(s, p) ==
  /\ status[s] = "proposed"
  /\ p \notin yes[s]
  /\ yes' = [yes EXCEPT ![s] = yes[s] \cup {p}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<status, pend, owner, active>>

Commit(s) ==
  /\ status[s] = "proposed"
  /\ yes[s] = Parts
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = pend[s]]
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![s] = "committed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pend, yes, active>>

Abort(s) ==
  /\ status[s] = "proposed"
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![s] = "free"]
  /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![s] = NULL]
  /\ yes' = [yes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, active>>

Release(s) ==
  /\ status[s] = "committed"
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = NULL]
  /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![s] = NULL]
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![s] = "free"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yes, active>>

Reconfig(s) ==
  /\ status[s] = "free"
  /\ IF s \in active THEN active' = active \ {s} ELSE active' = active \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<status, pend, yes, owner>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Slots, f \in Flights : Propose(s, f)
  \/ \E s \in Slots, p \in Parts : Vote(s, p)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Commit(s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Abort(s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Release(s)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Reconfig(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAlloc ==
  \A s1, s2 \in Slots :
    (s1 # s2 /\ owner[s1] # NULL /\ owner[s2] # NULL) => owner[s1] # owner[s2]
====
nl:
An air-traffic control system allocates runway landing slots to inbound flights
using a two-phase commit protocol across a set of tower participants. Each slot
begins free. A coordinator PROPOSES a free, currently-active slot for a flight,
but only if that flight is not already the owner of another committed slot and
is not already pending on some other proposed slot. Each participant then VOTES
yes on the proposal. Once every participant has voted yes, the coordinator
COMMITS, making the flight the owner of that slot. A proposal may instead be
ABORTED, returning the slot to free. A committed slot can later be RELEASED back
to free when the flight departs. Because runway capacity changes at runtime, a
RECONFIG action activates or deactivates a free slot; proposals may only target
active slots. Actions: Propose, Vote, Commit, Abort, Release, Reconfig.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct committed slots are ever owned by the same flight.

---- MODULE W4Od17m8p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Routers, Chutes, Zones, NULL

ZoneOf(c) == IF c <= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 2

VARIABLES czlock, cflock, step, held, heldZone, pace
vars == <<czlock, cflock, step, held, heldZone, pace>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ czlock \in [Zones -> Routers \cup {NULL}]
  /\ cflock \in [Chutes -> Routers \cup {NULL}]
  /\ step \in [Routers -> {"idle", "zoned", "holding"}]
  /\ held \in [Routers -> Chutes \cup {NULL}]
  /\ heldZone \in [Routers -> Zones \cup {NULL}]
  /\ pace \in [Routers -> {"ontime", "slow"}]

Init ==
  /\ czlock = [z \in Zones |-> NULL]
  /\ cflock = [c \in Chutes |-> NULL]
  /\ step = [r \in Routers |-> "idle"]
  /\ held = [r \in Routers |-> NULL]
  /\ heldZone = [r \in Routers |-> NULL]
  /\ pace = [r \in Routers |-> "ontime"]

AcquireZone(r, z) ==
  /\ step[r] = "idle"
  /\ czlock[z] = NULL
  /\ czlock' = [czlock EXCEPT ![z] = r]
  /\ heldZone' = [heldZone EXCEPT ![r] = z]
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![r] = "zoned"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cflock, held, pace>>

AcquireChute(r, c) ==
  /\ step[r] = "zoned"
  /\ heldZone[r] = ZoneOf(c)
  /\ cflock[c] = NULL
  /\ cflock' = [cflock EXCEPT ![c] = r]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![r] = c]
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![r] = "holding"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<czlock, heldZone, pace>>

ReleaseChute(r) ==
  /\ step[r] = "holding"
  /\ cflock' = [cflock EXCEPT ![held[r]] = NULL]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![r] = NULL]
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![r] = "zoned"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<czlock, heldZone, pace>>

ReleaseZone(r) ==
  /\ step[r] = "zoned"
  /\ czlock' = [czlock EXCEPT ![heldZone[r]] = NULL]
  /\ heldZone' = [heldZone EXCEPT ![r] = NULL]
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cflock, held, pace>>

Delay(r) ==
  /\ pace' = [pace EXCEPT ![r] = IF pace[r] = "ontime" THEN "slow" ELSE "ontime"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<czlock, cflock, step, held, heldZone>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Routers, z \in Zones : AcquireZone(r, z)
  \/ \E r \in Routers, c \in Chutes : AcquireChute(r, c)
  \/ \E r \in Routers : ReleaseChute(r)
  \/ \E r \in Routers : ReleaseZone(r)
  \/ \E r \in Routers : Delay(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ZoneExclusive ==
  \A c1, c2 \in Chutes :
    (cflock[c1] # NULL /\ cflock[c2] # NULL /\ ZoneOf(c1) = ZoneOf(c2))
      => cflock[c1] = cflock[c2]
====
nl:
An airport baggage router assigns bags to delivery chutes using hierarchical
two-level locking: chutes are grouped into zones, and a router must acquire the
coarse zone lock before it can acquire any fine chute lock inside that zone.
A router starts idle. ACQUIREZONE takes a free zone's coarse lock and moves the
router to "zoned". ACQUIRECHUTE, allowed only while zoned and only for a chute
whose zone the router already holds, takes that chute's fine lock and moves to
"holding". RELEASECHUTE frees the fine lock and returns to "zoned".
RELEASEZONE, allowed only when not holding any chute, frees the coarse lock and
returns to idle. Because a participant can be slow but never fails, a DELAY
action toggles a router between on-time and slow pacing; a slow router still
eventually proceeds and holds no locks hostage. Actions: AcquireZone,
AcquireChute, ReleaseChute, ReleaseZone, Delay.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any two chutes in the same zone that are both locked are held by the same router.

---- MODULE W4Od12m1p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Nodes, Units, NULL, RingSize

RingNext(n) == (n + 1) % RingSize

Range(sq) == {sq[i] : i \in DOMAIN sq}

VARIABLES token, inCS, want, log, pace
vars == <<token, inCS, want, log, pace>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ token \in Nodes
  /\ inCS \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ want \in [Nodes -> Units \cup {NULL}]
  /\ log \in Seq(Units)
  /\ pace \in [Nodes -> {"active", "slow"}]

Init ==
  /\ token = 0
  /\ inCS = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]
  /\ want = [n \in Nodes |-> NULL]
  /\ log = << >>
  /\ pace = [n \in Nodes |-> "active"]

Request(n, u) ==
  /\ want[n] = NULL
  /\ u \notin Range(log)
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![n] = u]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, inCS, log, pace>>

Enter(n) ==
  /\ token = n
  /\ ~inCS[n]
  /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, want, log, pace>>

Dispense(n) ==
  /\ inCS[n]
  /\ want[n] # NULL
  /\ want[n] \notin Range(log)
  /\ log' = Append(log, want[n])
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![n] = NULL]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, inCS, pace>>

Exit(n) ==
  /\ inCS[n]
  /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, want, log, pace>>

Pass(n) ==
  /\ token = n
  /\ ~inCS[n]
  /\ token' = RingNext(n)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, want, log, pace>>

Delay(n) ==
  /\ pace' = [pace EXCEPT ![n] = IF pace[n] = "active" THEN "slow" ELSE "active"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, inCS, want, log>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in Nodes, u \in Units : Request(n, u)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Enter(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Dispense(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Exit(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Pass(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Delay(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DispenseAtMostOnce ==
  \A i, j \in DOMAIN log : (i # j) => (log[i] # log[j])
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Nodes = {0, 1, 2}
  Units = {u1, u2}
  NULL = NULL
  RingSize = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DispenseAtMostOnce
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker coordinates nodes around a logical token ring so
that exactly one node at a time has exclusive access to release (irreversibly
dispense) a unit of blood. A single token circulates: PASS hands the token to
the next node in the ring, allowed only when the passing node is not in its
critical section. A node holding the token may ENTER its critical section. While
holding the token, a node first REQUESTs a specific not-yet-dispensed unit,
then DISPENSEs it, appending that unit to an append-only dispense log; a unit is
only appended if it is not already in the log, capturing the irreversible
"exactly once" nature of a transfusion. EXIT leaves the critical section so the
token can move on. Because a participant can be slow but never fails, a DELAY
action toggles a node between active and slow pacing without dropping the token.
Actions: Request, Enter, Dispense, Exit, Pass, Delay.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No blood unit appears more than once in the append-only dispense log.

---- MODULE W4Od16m9p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bins, Scripts, MaxEpoch, NULL

Msgs == [slot: Bins, script: Scripts, ep: 0..MaxEpoch]

VARIABLES epoch, alloc, pool, grantEp
vars == <<epoch, alloc, pool, grantEp>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ alloc \in [Bins -> Scripts \cup {NULL}]
  /\ pool \in SUBSET Msgs
  /\ grantEp \in [Bins -> 0..MaxEpoch]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ alloc = [b \in Bins |-> NULL]
  /\ pool = {}
  /\ grantEp = [b \in Bins |-> 0]

ScriptTaken(x) == \E b \in Bins : alloc[b] = x

Send(b, x) ==
  /\ LET m == [slot |-> b, script |-> x, ep |-> epoch] IN
       /\ m \notin pool
       /\ pool' = pool \cup {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, alloc, grantEp>>

Grant(m) ==
  /\ m \in pool
  /\ m.ep = epoch
  /\ alloc[m.slot] = NULL
  /\ ~ScriptTaken(m.script)
  /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![m.slot] = m.script]
  /\ grantEp' = [grantEp EXCEPT ![m.slot] = epoch]
  /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED epoch

Drop(m) ==
  /\ m \in pool
  /\ m.ep # epoch
  /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, alloc, grantEp>>

Reconfig ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, pool, grantEp>>

Release(b) ==
  /\ alloc[b] # NULL
  /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![b] = NULL]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, pool, grantEp>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bins, x \in Scripts : Send(b, x)
  \/ \E m \in pool : Grant(m)
  \/ \E m \in pool : Drop(m)
  \/ Reconfig
  \/ \E b \in Bins : Release(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleDispense ==
  \A b1, b2 \in Bins :
    (b1 # b2 /\ alloc[b1] # NULL /\ alloc[b2] # NULL) => alloc[b1] # alloc[b2]
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Bins = {b1, b2}
  Scripts = {x1, x2}
  MaxEpoch = 1
  NULL = NULL
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleDispense
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser routes prescriptions to dispensing bins under
epoch-numbered reconfiguration, where request messages can be reordered and
arrive in any order. Each dispense request is a message tagged with the bin, the
prescription (script), and the epoch current when it was SENT into the shared
message pool. GRANT nondeterministically picks any message from the pool and
commits it only if the message's epoch equals the current epoch, the target bin
is free, and that script is not already allocated to any bin; it then allocates
the bin to the script. A message whose epoch no longer matches the current epoch
is stale and gets DROPPED from the pool. RECONFIG bumps the epoch, invalidating
every in-flight message from the previous configuration. RELEASE frees an
allocated bin so its script can be re-dispensed later. Actions: Send, Grant,
Drop, Reconfig, Release.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct bins are ever allocated to the same prescription at once.

---- MODULE W4Od16m0p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Workers, Scripts, MaxCap, NULL

VARIABLES version, capacity, phase, rver, tgt, dispVer
vars == <<version, capacity, phase, rver, tgt, dispVer>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ version \in Nat
  /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCap
  /\ phase \in [Workers -> {"idle", "read", "committed"}]
  /\ rver \in [Workers -> Nat]
  /\ tgt \in [Workers -> Scripts \cup {NULL}]
  /\ dispVer \in [Scripts -> Nat \cup {NULL}]

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ capacity = MaxCap
  /\ phase = [w \in Workers |-> "idle"]
  /\ rver = [w \in Workers |-> 0]
  /\ tgt = [w \in Workers |-> NULL]
  /\ dispVer = [x \in Scripts |-> NULL]

Begin(w, x) ==
  /\ phase[w] = "idle"
  /\ rver' = [rver EXCEPT ![w] = version]
  /\ tgt' = [tgt EXCEPT ![w] = x]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = "read"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, capacity, dispVer>>

Commit(w) ==
  /\ phase[w] = "read"
  /\ rver[w] = version
  /\ capacity > 0
  /\ dispVer[tgt[w]] = NULL
  /\ dispVer' = [dispVer EXCEPT ![tgt[w]] = version]
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = "committed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rver, tgt>>

Retry(w) ==
  /\ phase[w] = "read"
  /\ rver[w] # version
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = "idle"]
  /\ tgt' = [tgt EXCEPT ![w] = NULL]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, capacity, rver, dispVer>>

Finish(w) ==
  /\ phase[w] = "committed"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = "idle"]
  /\ tgt' = [tgt EXCEPT ![w] = NULL]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, capacity, rver, dispVer>>

Restock ==
  /\ capacity < MaxCap
  /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, phase, rver, tgt, dispVer>>

Reduce ==
  /\ capacity > 0
  /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, phase, rver, tgt, dispVer>>

Next ==
  \/ \E w \in Workers, x \in Scripts : Begin(w, x)
  \/ \E w \in Workers : Commit(w)
  \/ \E w \in Workers : Retry(w)
  \/ \E w \in Workers : Finish(w)
  \/ Restock
  \/ Reduce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DispenseSerialized ==
  \A x1, x2 \in Scripts :
    (dispVer[x1] # NULL /\ dispVer[x2] # NULL /\ x1 # x2)
      => dispVer[x1] # dispVer[x2]
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Workers = {w1, w2}
  Scripts = {x1, x2}
  MaxCap = 1
  NULL = NULL
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DispenseSerialized
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser lets several workers dispense prescriptions
against a shared inventory using optimistic locking with retry. Each worker
BEGINs a transaction by optimistically reading the current shared version number
and choosing a target script, moving to the "read" phase. To COMMIT, a worker
must find that the version it read is still the current version (no concurrent
modification), that capacity remains, and that its target script has not already
been dispensed; committing records the commit version for that script, bumps the
shared version, consumes one unit of capacity, and irreversibly dispenses the
script. If the read version is stale, the worker RETRYs, abandoning its
transaction and returning to idle. FINISH resets a committed worker back to idle.
Because capacity changes at runtime, RESTOCK raises available capacity and REDUCE
lowers it, both within bounds. Actions: Begin, Commit, Retry, Finish, Restock,
Reduce.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct dispensed prescriptions share the same commit version, so each irreversible dispense occupies a unique serialization slot.

---- MODULE W4Od19m2p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Branches, AuthBranches, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES coord, pstate, pepoch, epoch
vars == <<coord, pstate, pepoch, epoch>>

PStates == {"idle", "prepared", "committed", "aborted"}
CStates == {"init", "preparing", "committed", "aborted"}

TypeOK ==
  /\ coord \in CStates
  /\ pstate \in [Branches -> PStates]
  /\ pepoch \in [Branches -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch

Init ==
  /\ coord = "init"
  /\ pstate = [b \in Branches |-> "idle"]
  /\ pepoch = [b \in Branches |-> 0]
  /\ epoch = 0

BeginPrepare ==
  /\ coord = "init"
  /\ coord' = "preparing"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pstate, pepoch, epoch>>

Vote(b) ==
  /\ coord = "preparing"
  /\ b \in AuthBranches
  /\ pepoch[b] = epoch
  /\ pstate[b] = "idle"
  /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![b] = "prepared"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, pepoch, epoch>>

Commit ==
  /\ coord = "preparing"
  /\ \A b \in AuthBranches : pstate[b] = "prepared"
  /\ coord' = "committed"
  /\ pstate' = [b \in Branches |-> IF b \in AuthBranches THEN "committed" ELSE pstate[b]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pepoch, epoch>>

Abort ==
  /\ coord = "preparing"
  /\ coord' = "aborted"
  /\ pstate' = [b \in Branches |-> IF pstate[b] = "prepared" THEN "aborted" ELSE pstate[b]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pepoch, epoch>>

Refresh(b) ==
  /\ pepoch[b] # epoch
  /\ pepoch' = [pepoch EXCEPT ![b] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, pstate, epoch>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ coord' = "init"
  /\ pstate' = [b \in Branches |-> "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED pepoch

Reset ==
  /\ coord \in {"committed", "aborted"}
  /\ coord' = "init"
  /\ pstate' = [b \in Branches |-> "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pepoch, epoch>>

Next ==
  \/ BeginPrepare
  \/ Commit
  \/ Abort
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ Reset
  \/ \E b \in Branches : Vote(b) \/ Refresh(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleAction ==
  \A b \in Branches :
    pstate[b] = "committed" => (b \in AuthBranches /\ pepoch[b] = epoch)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Branches = {b1, b2, b3}
  AuthBranches = {b1, b2}
  MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleAction
nl:
A library book reservation system coordinates a hold across several branch nodes using two-phase commit. Only authorized branches may participate in a reservation round, and each branch carries a membership epoch. The coordinator begins a prepare phase (BeginPrepare). An authorized branch whose epoch matches the coordinator's current epoch may cast a prepare vote (Vote). Once every authorized branch has voted prepared, the coordinator commits the reservation and marks those branches committed (Commit); otherwise it aborts the round and rolls back prepared branches (Abort). A branch that has fallen behind is slow but not failed: it can catch up to the current epoch at any time (Refresh). Membership can be reconfigured, which bumps the epoch and resets the round so that branches which have not refreshed become stale (Reconfigure). After a committed or aborted round the coordinator resets to begin again (Reset). A stale branch (epoch behind) or an unauthorized branch must never take part in a committed reservation.

  /\ Len(queue) <= Cap
  /\ owner \in Workers \cup {NULL}
  /\ wstate \in [Workers -> {"idle", "routing"}]
  /\ routed \in 0..MaxRouted

  /\ owner = NULL
  /\ wstate = [w \in Workers |-> "idle"]

  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, wstate, routed>>

Reorder ==
  /\ Len(queue) >= 2
  /\ queue' = <<queue[2], queue[1]>> \o SubSeq(queue, 3, Len(queue))
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, wstate, routed>>

Acquire(w) ==
  /\ owner = NULL
  /\ wstate[w] = "idle"
  /\ Len(queue) > 0
  /\ owner' = w
  /\ wstate' = [wstate EXCEPT ![w] = "routing"]
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED routed

  /\ owner = w
  /\ wstate[w] = "routing"
  /\ owner' = NULL
  /\ wstate' = [wstate EXCEPT ![w] = "idle"]
  /\ routed' = IF routed >= MaxRouted THEN 0 ELSE routed + 1

  \/ \E b \in Bags : Enqueue(b)
  \/ \E w \in Workers : Acquire(w) \/ Complete(w)

An airport baggage router feeds bags into a single critical routing chute that only one worker may operate at a time. Incoming bags wait in a bounded work queue that applies backpressure: a new bag can be enqueued only while the queue is below its capacity (Enqueue). Because bags arrive over an unreliable feed, queued messages can be reordered, swapping the order of the two frontmost bags (Reorder). When the worker finishes it completes the route, releases ownership of the chute, and returns to idle while a routed counter advances and wraps (Complete). The chute is a mutually exclusive resource: whoever is routing must be the recorded owner, and the recorded owner must be the one routing.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any worker in the routing state is the chute owner, and if the chute is owned that owner is the one routing, so at most one worker uses the chute at a time.

  /\ dstate[d] = "idle"
  /\ \E s \in Slots \ grantedSlots :

       /\ dstate' = [dstate EXCEPT ![d] = "proposed"]
       /\ coord' = "voting"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<held, grantedSlots>>

  /\ want[d] \notin grantedSlots

  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![d] = want[d]]
  /\ dstate' = [dstate EXCEPT ![d] = "holding"]
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![d] = NULL]
  /\ coord' = "idle"

  /\ dstate[d] = "proposed"
  /\ dstate' = [dstate EXCEPT ![d] = "idle"]
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![d] = NULL]
  /\ coord' = "idle"

  /\ grantedSlots' = grantedSlots \ {held[d]}
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![d] = NULL]
  /\ dstate' = [dstate EXCEPT ![d] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, want>>

  /\ dstate[d] = "holding"
  /\ grantedSlots' = grantedSlots \ {held[d]}
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![d] = NULL]
  /\ dstate' = [dstate EXCEPT ![d] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coord, want>>

    \/ Commit(d)
    \/ Abort(d)
    \/ Crash(d)
    \/ Recover(d)
    \/ Release(d)

A wildfire drone surveillance swarm allocates disjoint surveillance slots (grid cells) to drones through a two-phase-commit coordinator. When the coordinator is idle, a free drone proposes to take some slot that is not already granted, entering the voting phase (Propose). If the proposal cannot proceed the coordinator aborts it and the drone returns to idle (Abort). A bank's interbank settlement batch accepts settlement entries from several member banks up to a bounded capacity, using optimistic locking with retry. A bank first reads the current count of committed entries as its snapshot (ReadBatch). It then commits one entry using a compare-and-set: the commit succeeds only if the committed count still matches the snapshot it read and the count is strictly below the current capacity, adding one entry (CommitEntry). A wildfire surveillance drone swarm coordinates through epoch-numbered reconfiguration.
A global epoch counter names the currently valid configuration. Each drone keeps a
local view of which epoch it believes is current, and the swarm leader maintains, per
epoch, the roster of drones authorized to fly and observe in that epoch.

Actions:
- Reconfigure: the swarm leader advances the global epoch by one and publishes a fresh
  authorized roster for the new epoch (e.g. after a drone is lost or airspace changes).
- Sync: a drone updates its local view to match the current global epoch.
- Act: a drone performs a surveillance action. It may only do so if it is on the roster
  for the current epoch AND its local view is current (it is neither unauthorized nor
  operating on a stale, superseded configuration).
- AdminAct: a privileged admin override records a sanctioned surveillance action that is
  exempt from the ordinary rostering and freshness checks, available only while the
  override switch is engaged.
- ToggleAdmin: the operator engages or disengages the admin override switch.

Stale drones must resync before acting, and reconfiguration can drop drones from the
roster so that previously valid participants become unauthorized.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every recorded surveillance action was either an admin override or was
taken by a drone that was on the authorized roster for the epoch at which it acted.

VARIABLES ver, snap, reg, wlog, adminOn

    /\ snap \in [Procs -> Versions]
    /\ reg \in Procs \cup {NULL}
    /\ wlog \subseteq [num: 1..MaxVer, base: Versions, adm: BOOLEAN]
    /\ adminOn \in BOOLEAN

    /\ snap = [p \in Procs |-> 0]
    /\ reg = NULL
    /\ wlog = {}
    /\ adminOn = FALSE

\* A scheduler process reads the shared record, remembering the version it saw.
Read(p) ==
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![p] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, reg, wlog, adminOn>>

\* Compare-and-swap commit: succeeds only if the version is unchanged since the read,
\* so the update is applied on top of the exact version it was computed against.
CAS(p) ==
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ snap[p] = ver
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ reg' = p
    /\ wlog' = wlog \cup {[num |-> ver + 1, base |-> snap[p], adm |-> FALSE]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, adminOn>>

\* bypassing the ordinary CAS contention but still building on the current version.

    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ reg' = p
    /\ wlog' = wlog \cup {[num |-> ver + 1, base |-> ver, adm |-> TRUE]}

    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, snap, reg, wlog>>

    \/ \E p \in Procs : CAS(p)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : AdminWrite(p)
    \/ ToggleAdmin

\* on top of the version immediately preceding it, so no concurrent write was clobbered.

A hospital operating-room scheduler protects a shared booking record with a
compare-and-swap (CAS) register. The record carries a version number that increases by
one on every successful write. Scheduler processes read the record, compute a proposed
change off-line, and then attempt to commit.

Actions:
- Read: a scheduler process reads the shared record and remembers the version it saw.
- CAS: a process attempts to commit its computed change. The commit succeeds only if the
  current version still equals the version the process last read; on success it writes the
  new booking and bumps the version by one. If some other process wrote in the meantime,
  the compare fails and no update is lost.
- AdminWrite: a privileged admin override force-writes the record even under contention,
  but it re-reads the record live so its write still builds on the current version.
- ToggleAdmin: the operator engages or disengages the admin override switch.

Because a CAS only commits when its base version is still current, a stale write can never
silently overwrite a concurrent committed update.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every committed write, unless it is an admin override, was applied on top
of the version immediately preceding it, so no concurrent update is ever lost.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Books, Readers, NULL, MaxTime, Lease

    /\ allocatedTo \in [Books -> Readers \cup {NULL}]
    /\ expiry \in [Books -> 0..(MaxTime + Lease)]
    /\ holds \in [Readers -> SUBSET Books]
    /\ adminOn \in BOOLEAN

    /\ clock = 0
    /\ allocatedTo = [b \in Books |-> NULL]
    /\ expiry = [b \in Books |-> 0]
    /\ holds = [r \in Readers |-> {}]
    /\ adminOn = FALSE

\* A reader takes a lease on a book that is free or whose prior lease has expired.
\* Reclaiming an expired lease also strips the book from the previous holder's set.
Grant(r, b) ==
    /\ (allocatedTo[b] = NULL) \/ (expiry[b] <= clock)
    /\ LET prev == allocatedTo[b] IN
         holds' = [x \in Readers |->
                     IF x = r THEN holds[x] \cup {b}
                     ELSE IF x = prev THEN holds[x] \ {b}
                     ELSE holds[x]]
    /\ allocatedTo' = [allocatedTo EXCEPT ![b] = r]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![b] = clock + Lease]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, adminOn>>

\* A reader voluntarily returns a book it holds.
Release(r, b) ==
    /\ b \in holds[r]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![r] = holds[r] \ {b}]
    /\ allocatedTo' = [allocatedTo EXCEPT ![b] = NULL]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, expiry, adminOn>>

\* Wall-clock time advances, which lets leases expire and become reclaimable.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxTime
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocatedTo, expiry, holds, adminOn>>

\* Privileged admin override: revokes a book from wherever it is held and frees the slot.
AdminRevoke(b) ==
    /\ adminOn
    /\ allocatedTo' = [allocatedTo EXCEPT ![b] = NULL]
    /\ holds' = [x \in Readers |-> holds[x] \ {b}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, expiry, adminOn>>

ToggleAdmin ==
    /\ adminOn' = ~adminOn
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, allocatedTo, expiry, holds>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Readers, b \in Books : Grant(r, b)
    \/ \E r \in Readers, b \in Books : Release(r, b)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E b \in Books : AdminRevoke(b)
    \/ ToggleAdmin

\* No double allocation: if a reader believes it holds a book, the central register
\* agrees the book is allocated to exactly that reader (so no two readers can hold one).

    \A r \in Readers, b \in Books : b \in holds[r] => allocatedTo[b] = r

A library book reservation system allocates copies (slots) to readers using lease-based
ownership with expiry. A central register records, for each book, which reader currently
holds it and when that lease expires. Each reader also tracks the set of books it believes
it holds. A global clock drives lease expiry.

Actions:
- Grant: a reader takes a lease on a book that is currently free or whose lease has already
  expired. The book is allocated to the reader with a fresh expiry time. When an expired
  lease is reclaimed, the book is simultaneously stripped from the previous holder's set,
  so it is never counted as held by two readers at once.
- Release: a reader voluntarily returns a book it holds, freeing the slot.
- Tick: wall-clock time advances, allowing existing leases to expire and become reclaimable.
- AdminRevoke: a privileged admin override forcibly reclaims a book from whoever holds it
  and frees the slot, available only while the override switch is engaged.
- ToggleAdmin: the librarian engages or disengages the admin override switch.

Reclaiming an expired lease always clears the stale holder, so a book is never granted to a
new reader while another still counts it as theirs.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a reader believes it holds a book, the central register shows that
book allocated to exactly that reader, so no slot is ever double-allocated.

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxSeq

VARIABLES token, seq, lockState, prepared, chain

SeqNums == 1..MaxSeq

    /\ seq \in SeqNums
    /\ lockState \in 0..MaxSeq
    /\ prepared \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxSeq]
    /\ chain \subseteq [num: 2..MaxSeq, base: SeqNums, by: Nodes]

    /\ token \in Nodes
    /\ seq = 1
    /\ lockState = 0
    /\ prepared = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]

\* The exclusive-access token rotates around the ring to the next lock node.
PassToken(n) ==
    /\ token = n
    /\ \E m \in Nodes \ {n} : token' = m

\* A node prepares an update by reading the current record sequence number. A slow node
\* may prepare well before it ever commits, leaving its prepared value behind the record.

    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![n] = seq]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, seq, lockState, chain>>

\* not advanced since it prepared, so its write builds on the immediately prior record.

    /\ token = n
    /\ prepared[n] = seq
    /\ seq < MaxSeq
    /\ seq' = seq + 1
    /\ lockState' = seq + 1
    /\ chain' = chain \cup {[num |-> seq + 1, base |-> prepared[n], by |-> n]}
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![n] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token>>

\* A slow node discards a prepared value it never committed (it fell behind).
Discard(n) ==
    /\ prepared[n] # 0
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![n] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, seq, lockState, chain>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : PassToken(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Prepare(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Commit(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Discard(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: every committed change to the shared lock record was applied on top
\* of the record sequence immediately preceding it (its base is exactly one below it).
NoLostUpdate ==
    \A c \in chain : c.base = c.num - 1

  Nodes = {n1, n2}
  MaxSeq = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
A smart-home door-lock network shares a single lock-configuration record. Exclusive write
access is granted by a token ring: a single token rotates among the lock nodes, and only
the node currently holding the token may commit a change. The shared record carries a
sequence number that increases by one on each committed change. A node can be slow (delayed)
but not failed, so the token always keeps circulating.

Actions:
- PassToken: the current token holder rotates the token to the next node in the ring.
- Prepare: a node prepares an update by reading the record's current sequence number and
  remembering it. A slow node may prepare long before it commits.
- Commit: the token holder applies its prepared update, but only if the record's sequence
  number has not advanced since it prepared. On success it writes the new lock state and
  bumps the sequence, so the change is built on the immediately prior record.
- Discard: a slow node throws away a stale prepared value it never got to commit because
  the record moved on without it.

Because a commit is refused whenever the node's prepared sequence has fallen behind the
record, a delayed node can never clobber an update committed while it was slow.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every committed change to the shared lock record was applied on top of the
record sequence immediately preceding it, so no update is ever lost.

CONSTANTS Jobs, Workers, NULL, Cap

VARIABLES pending, assigned, completed, crashed, source

vars == <<pending, assigned, completed, crashed, source>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ pending \subseteq Jobs
    /\ assigned \in [Jobs -> Workers \cup {NULL}]
    /\ completed \subseteq Jobs
    /\ crashed \in [Workers -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ source \subseteq Jobs

Init ==
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ assigned = [j \in Jobs |-> NULL]
    /\ completed = {}
    /\ crashed = [w \in Workers |-> FALSE]
    /\ source = Jobs

\* A new dispatch request enters the bounded queue; backpressure blocks it when full.
Enqueue(j) ==
    /\ j \in source
    /\ Cardinality(pending) < Cap
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {j}
    /\ source' = source \ {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, completed, crashed>>

\* A live elevator claims a queued, unassigned dispatch.
Claim(w, j) ==
    /\ ~crashed[w]
    /\ j \in pending
    /\ assigned[j] = NULL
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![j] = w]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, completed, crashed, source>>

\* A live elevator performs the irreversible dispatch, then removes the job from the
\* queue and clears its assignment so it can never be picked up or dispatched again.
Complete(w, j) ==
    /\ ~crashed[w]
    /\ assigned[j] = w
    /\ j \in pending
    /\ j \notin completed
    /\ completed' = completed \cup {j}
    /\ pending' = pending \ {j}
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![j] = NULL]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, source>>

\* An elevator crashes silently: its in-flight claims are released back to the queue,
\* but no completed dispatch is affected (completed jobs already left the queue).
Crash(w) ==
    /\ ~crashed[w]
    /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![w] = TRUE]
    /\ assigned' = [j \in Jobs |-> IF assigned[j] = w THEN NULL ELSE assigned[j]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, completed, source>>

\* A crashed elevator is brought back online.
Recover(w) ==
    /\ crashed[w]
    /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![w] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, assigned, completed, source>>

Next ==
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Enqueue(j)
    \/ \E w \in Workers, j \in Jobs : Claim(w, j)
    \/ \E w \in Workers, j \in Jobs : Complete(w, j)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Crash(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Recover(w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* At most once: any job whose irreversible dispatch has been performed is neither still
\* in the queue nor assigned to any elevator, so it can never be dispatched a second time.
AtMostOnce ==
    \A j \in completed : (j \notin pending) /\ (assigned[j] = NULL)

  Workers = {w1, w2}
  NULL = NULL
  Cap = 1
INIT Init

INVARIANT AtMostOnce
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper dispatches cars to floor-call requests through a bounded
work queue with backpressure. Incoming requests are enqueued only while the queue has room;
when it is full, backpressure blocks new arrivals. Elevators claim queued requests and then
perform the physical dispatch, which is an irreversible action that must happen at most once
per request. One elevator can crash silently.

Actions:
- Enqueue: a pending floor-call request enters the bounded queue, unless the queue is at
  capacity (backpressure), in which case the request waits outside the queue.
- Claim: a live elevator claims a queued, unassigned request so it alone will service it.
- Complete: a live elevator performs the irreversible dispatch for a request it has claimed
  and that has not already been completed; it then removes the request from the queue and
  clears its assignment, so the request can never be claimed or dispatched again.
- Crash: an elevator crashes silently. Any request it had merely claimed (not yet
  dispatched) is released back to the queue for another elevator; already-completed
  dispatches are untouched because completed requests have already left the queue.
- Recover: a crashed elevator is brought back online.

A crash can only re-expose a claim that never reached dispatch, so no request is ever
dispatched twice even across silent failures.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any request whose irreversible dispatch has been performed is neither in
the queue nor assigned to any elevator, so it can never be dispatched a second time.

nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker seats players into a single shared lobby that has
a bounded capacity, and that capacity may be reconfigured while the lobby is live.
Because seating touches both the whole lobby and an individual seat, admission uses
hierarchical locking: a joining player first grabs the coarse lobby lock, then grabs
the fine seat lock, and only then commits into a seat.

Actions:
- GrabCoarse(p): an idle player takes the coarse lobby lock when it is free.
- GrabFine(p): a player holding the coarse lock takes the free fine seat lock.
- Commit(p): a player holding the fine lock is seated only if the current occupancy
  is strictly below capacity; committing releases both the coarse and fine locks.
- Leave(p): a seated player leaves the lobby and frees its seat.
- Release(p): a player that acquired locks but has not committed aborts and releases
  whichever locks it holds (recovery so no one is stuck holding a lock forever).
- Resize: the operator changes the lobby capacity at runtime to any allowed value,
  but never below the number of currently seated players.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of seated players never exceeds the current capacity.

nl:
A warehouse robot fleet drains a fixed pool of jobs. Jobs start in a backlog, flow
through a bounded work queue that applies backpressure (nothing can be enqueued once
the queue is full), get carried by robots, and end up finished. A robot may be slow
but never fails outright: while slow it makes no progress, yet it never drops the job
it is carrying, so no job is ever lost or duplicated.

Actions:
- Enqueue: move one job from the backlog into the queue, only while the queue has
  room (backpressure blocks it when full).
- Pick(r): a ready robot not already carrying takes one job out of the queue.
- Complete(r): a ready robot carrying a job finishes it, incrementing the done count.
- Stall(r): a ready robot becomes slow (temporarily stops making progress).
- Resume(r): a slow robot becomes ready again, still holding any job it had.

fixed constant at all times.

and finished always sums to the fixed total.

A stock exchange opening auction is driven by a single elected leader per epoch, with
failover: any node can win a fresh election that bumps the global epoch and makes it
the new leader. Followers must catch up to the current epoch before they can be trusted.
Only the leader of the current epoch may drive auction steps; a deposed or stale leader
(one whose known epoch lags the global epoch) must never act. The auction's capacity may
also be reconfigured at runtime, but only by the legitimate current leader.

Actions:
- Elect(n): node n wins a new election, incrementing the epoch, becoming leader, and
  synchronizing its own known epoch; the record of who has acted this epoch is cleared.
- Sync(n): a lagging node advances its known epoch up to the current global epoch.
- RunAuction(n): the current, up-to-date leader performs an auction step and is recorded
  as having authored an action in this epoch.
- Resize(n): the current, up-to-date leader changes the auction capacity at runtime and
  is recorded as having authored an action in this epoch.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every node recorded as having acted in the current epoch is the current
leader and has a known epoch equal to the global epoch.

    /\ ver \in [Blocks -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ reqs \subseteq Msgs

    /\ occ = [b \in Blocks |-> IF b = 0 THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ ver = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
    /\ reqs = {}
    /\ retries = 0

Propose(b) ==
    /\ occ[b] > 0
    /\ reqs' = reqs \cup {[frm |-> b, obs |-> ver[b]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, ver, retries>>

Commit(m) ==
    /\ m \in reqs
    /\ occ[m.frm] > 0
    /\ m.obs = ver[m.frm]
    /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![m.frm] = @ - 1, ![Nxt(m.frm)] = @ + 1]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![m.frm] = (@ + 1) % (MaxVer + 1)]
    /\ reqs' = reqs \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED retries

    /\ m.obs # ver[m.frm]
    /\ reqs' = reqs \ {m}
    /\ retries' = IF retries < MaxRetry THEN retries + 1 ELSE retries
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, ver>>

    /\ retries > 0
    /\ retries' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, ver, reqs>>

    \/ \E m \in reqs : Reject(m)

    Blocks = {0, 1, 2}
    Total = 2
    MaxVer = 2
    MaxRetry = 2

nl:
A subway signalling block system moves a fixed set of trains around a loop of track
blocks. A train advances from its block to the next block using optimistic locking:
a controller reads the current version of a block and issues a move request carrying
that observed version. Requests travel as messages that may be delivered and applied
in any order (reordered). A move commits only if the observed version still matches
the block's current version (compare-and-swap); otherwise it is a stale request and is
rejected, to be retried later. Trains are neither created nor destroyed; the total
number of trains on the loop is constant.

Actions:
- Propose(b): read block b's version and enqueue a move request from b (b must be
  occupied). Requests form an unordered set, so they may be applied out of order.
- Commit(m): apply a pending move whose observed version still matches and whose source
  block is occupied; one train leaves the source block and enters the next block, and the
  source block's version is bumped.
- Reject(m): discard a pending move whose observed version no longer matches (stale due
  to reordering or a concurrent commit); a bounded retry counter is bumped.
- ClearRetries: reset the retry counter (always available so the system never deadlocks).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of trains summed over all blocks always equals the
fixed total.

nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser has one physical dispensing head, a critical resource
that must be used by at most one prescription at a time. Before a prescription may take
the head, it must collect a quorum of approver votes. Approvers vote independently and
their votes arrive in any order (reordered); a ballot simply accumulates the set of
approvers who have voted so far. Only after reaching quorum, and only while the head is
free, may a prescription seize the head and dispense.

Actions:
- OpenBallot(r): an idle prescription starts collecting votes, resetting its ballot.
- CastVote(r, a): approver a records its vote on prescription r's open ballot; because
  the ballot is a set, votes may be recorded in any order.
- Dispense(r): a prescription that has reached quorum seizes the free dispensing head
  and begins dispensing.
- Finish(r): the dispensing prescription completes, releases the head, clears its ballot,
  and is recorded as the last served.
- AbortBallot(r): a prescription still collecting votes gives up and returns to idle
  (recovery so voting can never wedge the system).

head and reached the required quorum of votes.

---- MODULE W4Od13m7p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Machines, Cells

VARIABLES occ, claimed, snap, phase
vars == <<occ, claimed, snap, phase>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ occ \subseteq Cells
    /\ claimed \in [Machines -> SUBSET Cells]
    /\ snap \in [Machines -> SUBSET Cells]
    /\ phase \in [Machines -> {"idle", "armed"}]

Init ==
    /\ occ = {}
    /\ claimed = [m \in Machines |-> {}]
    /\ snap = [m \in Machines |-> {}]
    /\ phase = [m \in Machines |-> "idle"]

\* A machine reads the shared compare-and-swap register (the set of occupied
\* cells of the bounded vending bin) into a private snapshot.
Read(m) ==
    /\ phase[m] = "idle"
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![m] = occ]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "armed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, claimed>>

\* Restock: CAS succeeds only if the register still equals the snapshot; the
\* machine occupies one free cell, recording the same cell in its own claim.
Claim(m) ==
    /\ phase[m] = "armed"
    /\ occ = snap[m]
    /\ occ # Cells
    /\ \E c \in Cells \ occ :
        /\ occ' = occ \cup {c}
        /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![m] = claimed[m] \cup {c}]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

\* Dispense: CAS succeeds only if the register still matches the snapshot; the
\* machine frees one of its own claimed cells from both the register and claim.
Release(m) ==
    /\ phase[m] = "armed"
    /\ occ = snap[m]
    /\ claimed[m] # {}
    /\ \E c \in claimed[m] :
        /\ occ' = occ \ {c}
        /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![m] = claimed[m] \ {c}]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

\* Reordering: if another machine's update landed first (snapshot is stale),
\* or there is nothing to do, the attempt is abandoned and later retried.
Retry(m) ==
    /\ phase[m] = "armed"
    /\ \/ occ # snap[m]
       \/ (occ = Cells /\ claimed[m] = {})
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, claimed, snap>>

Next == \E m \in Machines:
    \/ Read(m)
    \/ Claim(m)
    \/ Release(m)
    \/ Retry(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity is never exceeded: every cell a machine believes it has
\* claimed is actually marked occupied in the shared register, so machines can
\* only ever hold cells backed by the single register and can never
\* over-subscribe the bin beyond its fixed set of cells.
ClaimsBacked == \A m \in Machines : claimed[m] \subseteq occ

nl:
A network of vending machines shares one bounded stock bin whose occupancy
is kept in a single compare-and-swap (CAS) register: the set of currently
occupied cells. Each machine first reads the register into a private
snapshot (Read). To restock it performs a CAS that occupies one free cell
(Claim), recording that cell in its own claim set; the CAS commits only if
the register still equals the machine's snapshot. To dispense it performs a
CAS that frees one of its own claimed cells (Release), again only if the
register still matches its snapshot.

Because the network reorders messages, another machine's update may land
first, leaving a machine with a stale snapshot; in that case, or when there
is nothing useful to do, the attempt is abandoned and retried later
(Retry). Every machine can always read again, so the network never
deadlocks. Since a cell is occupied only when it is free, no two machines
ever claim the same cell, and the bin's fixed set of cells bounds capacity.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every cell a machine has claimed is actually marked occupied in the shared register, so machines never over-subscribe the bin beyond its bounded set of cells.

---- MODULE W4Od2m1p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS N

Robots == 0 .. (N - 1)
Succ(r) == (r + 1) % N

VARIABLES holder, mode, wants, slow
vars == <<holder, mode, wants, slow>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in Robots
    /\ mode \in [Robots -> {"idle", "eating"}]
    /\ wants \in [Robots -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ slow \in [Robots -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ holder = 0
    /\ mode = [r \in Robots |-> "idle"]
    /\ wants = [r \in Robots |-> FALSE]
    /\ slow = [r \in Robots |-> FALSE]

\* A robot signals it wants the shared resource.
Request(r) ==
    /\ ~wants[r]
    /\ mode[r] = "idle"
    /\ wants' = [wants EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, mode, slow>>

\* Only the token holder may enter the critical section.
Enter(r) ==
    /\ wants[r]
    /\ holder = r
    /\ mode[r] = "idle"
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![r] = "eating"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, wants, slow>>

\* A robot leaves the critical section.
Exit(r) ==
    /\ mode[r] = "eating"
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
    /\ wants' = [wants EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, slow>>

\* The token advances around the ring, but never while its holder is eating.
Pass(r) ==
    /\ holder = r
    /\ mode[r] # "eating"
    /\ ~slow[r]
    /\ holder' = Succ(r)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<mode, wants, slow>>

\* A robot may become slow (delaying its token pass) or recover from it;
\* being slow never drops the token, so mutual exclusion is preserved.
SetSlow(r) ==
    /\ ~slow[r]
    /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, mode, wants>>

Recover(r) ==
    /\ slow[r]
    /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, mode, wants>>

Next == \E r \in Robots:
    \/ Request(r)
    \/ Enter(r)
    \/ Exit(r)
    \/ Pass(r)
    \/ SetSlow(r)
    \/ Recover(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Mutual exclusion: any robot inside the critical section must currently
\* hold the single token, so at most one robot can be eating at a time.
MutexByToken == \A r \in Robots : mode[r] = "eating" => holder = r
====

CONSTANTS
    N = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutexByToken
nl:
A fleet of warehouse robots is arranged in a ring and shares one critical
resource (a charging bay). Exclusive access is granted by a single token
that circulates around the ring. A robot that needs the resource raises a
request (Request). Only the robot currently holding the token may enter
the critical section (Enter); when finished it leaves (Exit). The token
advances to the next robot in the ring (Pass), but never while its current
holder is eating in the critical section.

A robot can be slow but not failed: it may enter a slow state (SetSlow) in
which it delays passing the token, and later recover (Recover). Slowness
only postpones the pass; it never loses or duplicates the token, so at any
moment either SetSlow or Recover is enabled for every robot and the system
never deadlocks.

SAFETY PROPERTY: any robot in the critical section must hold the single token, so at most one robot is ever in the critical section.

---- MODULE W4Od0m2p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Parts

VARIABLES vote, decided, bus, operated
vars == <<vote, decided, bus, operated>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ vote \in [Parts -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ decided \in {"none", "commit", "abort"}
    /\ bus \subseteq Parts
    /\ operated \in [Parts -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ vote = [p \in Parts |-> "none"]
    /\ decided = "none"
    /\ bus = {}
    /\ operated = [p \in Parts |-> FALSE]

\* Phase 1: each participating operating room votes yes or no.
CastVote(p) ==
    /\ vote[p] = "none"
    /\ \E v \in {"yes", "no"} : vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![p] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<decided, bus, operated>>

\* Phase 2: the coordinator commits only if every room voted yes, and
\* broadcasts the irreversible go-ahead onto the message bus.
DecideCommit ==
    /\ decided = "none"
    /\ \A p \in Parts : vote[p] = "yes"
    /\ decided' = "commit"
    /\ bus' = Parts
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, operated>>

\* The coordinator aborts if any room voted no; no go-ahead is ever sent.
DecideAbort ==
    /\ decided = "none"
    /\ \E p \in Parts : vote[p] = "no"
    /\ decided' = "abort"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, bus, operated>>

\* Messages may be reordered: any queued go-ahead may be delivered in any
\* order, causing that room to perform its irreversible incision exactly once.
Deliver(p) ==
    /\ p \in bus
    /\ ~operated[p]
    /\ operated' = [operated EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ bus' = bus \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, decided>>

\* Once the transaction has resolved and all go-aheads are consumed, the
\* round resets for the next scheduling cycle, so no state is terminal.
Reset ==
    /\ decided # "none"
    /\ bus = {}
    /\ vote' = [p \in Parts |-> "none"]
    /\ decided' = "none"
    /\ operated' = [p \in Parts |-> FALSE]
    /\ bus' = {}

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Parts : CastVote(p)
    \/ DecideCommit
    \/ DecideAbort
    \/ \E p \in Parts : Deliver(p)
    \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* An irreversible action happens at most once (and only under commit): if
\* the transaction aborted, no room has performed the irreversible incision.
AbortIsSafe == (decided = "abort") => (\A p \in Parts : ~operated[p])
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Parts = {r1, r2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AbortIsSafe
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler coordinates an irreversible surgery
across several rooms using two-phase commit. In phase one every room casts
a vote (CastVote), yes or no. In phase two the coordinator commits only if
all rooms voted yes (DecideCommit), broadcasting an irreversible go-ahead
onto the message bus; if any room voted no it aborts (DecideAbort) and no
go-ahead is ever sent.

Because messages can be reordered, queued go-aheads are delivered in any
order (Deliver); each room that receives its go-ahead performs its
irreversible incision exactly once, guarded so it can never repeat. After
the transaction resolves and every go-ahead has been consumed, the round
resets for the next scheduling cycle (Reset), so the system never
deadlocks.

SAFETY PROPERTY: if the transaction aborted, no room has performed the irreversible incision, so the irreversible action happens at most once and only under a commit.

---- MODULE W4Od19m8p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Readers, Slots, NULL

Owners == Readers \cup {NULL}

VARIABLES shelf, hold, grant, live
vars == <<shelf, hold, grant, live>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ shelf \in Owners
    /\ hold \in [Slots -> Owners]
    /\ grant \in [Slots -> Owners]
    /\ live \in [Slots -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ shelf = NULL
    /\ hold = [s \in Slots |-> NULL]
    /\ grant = [s \in Slots |-> NULL]
    /\ live = [s \in Slots |-> TRUE]

\* Coarse lock: a reader must first take the shelf-level lock.
LockShelf(r) ==
    /\ shelf = NULL
    /\ shelf' = r
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, grant, live>>

\* Fine lock: only the shelf holder may lock an active, unheld slot.
LockSlot(r) ==
    /\ shelf = r
    /\ \E s \in Slots :
        /\ live[s]
        /\ hold[s] = NULL
        /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![s] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, grant, live>>

\* A slot is reserved (allocated) only by the reader that holds its fine lock.
Allocate(r) ==
    /\ \E s \in Slots :
        /\ hold[s] = r
        /\ grant[s] = NULL
        /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![s] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, hold, live>>

\* Releasing a slot drops its reservation and its fine lock together.
ReleaseSlot(r) ==
    /\ \E s \in Slots :
        /\ hold[s] = r
        /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![s] = NULL]
        /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![s] = NULL]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, live>>

\* The coarse lock is released only after the reader holds no fine lock.
ReleaseShelf(r) ==
    /\ shelf = r
    /\ \A s \in Slots : hold[s] # r
    /\ shelf' = NULL
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, grant, live>>

\* Capacity changes at runtime: a free, unlocked slot may be retired, and a
\* retired slot may be brought back into service.
Retire ==
    /\ \E s \in Slots :
        /\ live[s]
        /\ hold[s] = NULL
        /\ grant[s] = NULL
        /\ live' = [live EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, hold, grant>>

Restore ==
    /\ \E s \in Slots :
        /\ ~live[s]
        /\ live' = [live EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, hold, grant>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Readers : LockShelf(r)
    \/ \E r \in Readers : LockSlot(r)
    \/ \E r \in Readers : Allocate(r)
    \/ \E r \in Readers : ReleaseSlot(r)
    \/ \E r \in Readers : ReleaseShelf(r)
    \/ Retire
    \/ Restore

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: a reserved slot is always held by the very reader it
\* is reserved for; since the fine lock is single-valued, the same slot can
\* never be allocated to two readers at once.
NoDoubleAlloc == \A s \in Slots : grant[s] # NULL => hold[s] = grant[s]
====

CONSTANTS
    Readers = {ra, rb}
    Slots = {s1, s2}
    NULL = NULL
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAlloc
nl:
A library book-reservation system hands out copies (slots) of a title to
readers using hierarchical locking: a coarse shelf-level lock must be taken
before any fine slot-level lock. A reader first takes the shelf lock
(LockShelf). While holding it, the reader may lock an active, currently
unheld slot (LockSlot). A slot is reserved for a reader (Allocate) only if
that reader holds the slot's fine lock. Releasing a slot (ReleaseSlot)
drops both its reservation and its fine lock together, and the shelf lock
is released (ReleaseShelf) only once the reader holds no fine locks.

Capacity changes at runtime: a free, unlocked, unreserved slot may be
retired from service (Retire), and a retired slot may later be restored
(Restore). Because a retired slot can always be restored and locks can
always be released, the system never deadlocks.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every reserved slot is held by exactly the reader it is reserved for, so the same slot is never allocated to two different readers.
